mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates a signed difference to another difference, translate it directly as (A - B) = (C - D) preserving the order and sign.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever you encounter a sentence of the form 'the number of X that Y has more than Z is equal to the difference between the number of A and B' or similar.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has more than Y' as |X - Y| = N instead of X - Y = N.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person, set that person's current count to the given number, overwriting any previous value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence states 'Person has N items' (or similar).
mathgap.example: Treating 'Leanne has 68 peaches' as a starting count and ignoring later transfers that may change it.

mathgap.title: Non‑negative integer check
mathgap.principle: All item counts must be non‑negative integers; discard any solution that yields a negative or fractional count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving equations, verify that each variable is a whole number ≥ 0.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution where a person ends up with -3 peaches.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For conditional transfers, first evaluate the condition using the current counts; only if the condition holds, apply the transfer.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'If X has more than Y, X gives Z to Y' or similar.
mathgap.example: Applying a transfer regardless of the condition, leading to incorrect counts.

mathgap.title: Redistribution equalization handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says two persons redistribute items to ensure each has an equal amount, pool their items and split evenly; any remainder is handled according to the problem rules.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering sentences like 'X and Y redistribute their items equally'.
mathgap.example: Leaving the original person with some items after a redistribution that should equalize both counts.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'X has N more than Y' as X - Y = N (i.e., X = Y + N) and 'X has N fewer than Y' as X - Y = -N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence uses 'more' or 'fewer' to compare counts.
mathgap.example: Misreading 'X has 5 more than Y' as X = Y - 5.

mathgap.title: Split-all handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X splits all the items she owns equally among Y and Z', give each of Y and Z half of X's current count and set X's count to zero.
mathgap.example: Leaving X with some items after a split‑all operation.

mathgap.title: Targeted constraint extraction for queried variable
mathgap.principle: When the goal is to find a specific person's count, first collect all statements that directly involve that person, and then focus on those constraints, ignoring unrelated ones.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem asks for the count of a particular individual.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system of equations when only a few constraints involve the queried person.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling with updated counts
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver; subsequent statements refer to these updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a 'X gives N items to Y' sentence is present.
mathgap.example: Evaluating a later comparison using the giver's original count instead of the reduced count after a prior transfer.

mathgap.title: Substitution of known signed differences into signed difference equalities
mathgap.principle: When a signed difference equality involves a difference that is already known from a direct 'X has N more/fewer than Y' statement, substitute that known value into the equality to simplify and solve for the remaining variables, rather than treating the equality as an absolute difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever you have an equation of the form (A - B) = (C - D) and you already know the numeric value of (A - B) or (C - D) from a previous direct comparison.
mathgap.example: Treating '(Hershel - Eva) = (Silas - Leanne)' as an absolute difference and not substituting the known value 'Hershel - Eva = 2', leading to ambiguous solutions.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often interprets 'X has N more than Y' as |X - Y| = N, losing sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the sign: translate 'X has N more than Y' as X - Y = N, and use signed difference equalities accordingly.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may treat all transfers as simultaneous, applying them after all other statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when encountered, updating counts before processing subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may think a direct count assignment sets the initial count only, not the final count after later transfers.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct count assignments as setting the current count at that point, which may be overridden by later transfers if any.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increase by N times' as addition rather than multiplication
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase 'increase by N times' is often read as 'add N' instead of 'multiply by N'.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'increase by N times' as multiplying the current count by N.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting split-all statements as leaving the original person with zero even when they are a recipient
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may think the original person retains some items after a split‑all, contrary to the definition.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When 'X splits all items among Y and Z', give each of Y and Z half of X's count and set X's count to zero.
